papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of objectives (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) has been developed and applied across vision, language, retrieval, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection (or synthesis), and task‑aware design choices. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and principled methods for heterogeneous architectures and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression (but Not a Standalone Cure)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, retrieval, detection, and healthcare shows KD routinely enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and careful objective and architecture design. Best practice treats KD as the central, configurable element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly addresses data scarcity, distribution shift, privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single trick into a broad, practical family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or privacy-aware models while retaining much of their performance. The techniques differ by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel statistics), how the transfer is staged (offline teacher-student, online/co-distillation, data-free/zero-shot, few-shot), and which complementary strategies are used (projectors, mixup/data augmentation, pruning, or architecture-aware design). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as information transfer and as a regularizer; success depends critically on choices about teacher signals, student capacity, the availability and nature of data, and task-specific design. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under limited or private data, preventing transfer of teacher errors, adapting to heterogeneous or federated settings, and scaling distillation to very large models and complex structured-output tasks.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from one or more teacher models to a student. A rich taxonomy of KD methods exists—output (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, self- and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and adversarial/sample-generation approaches—applied across classification, generation, translation, retrieval, graph learning, detection, and federated settings. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the form of transferred signals, the availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and choices about layer mapping and optimization. Outstanding challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, distribution shift, and reliably distilling structured or rare outputs; promising directions emphasize task-aware signal selection, many-to-many layer mappings, adversarial/data-free synthesis, teacher-free or meta-learned schemes, and tighter integration of KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance when objectives, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen to match task and deployment requirements. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on low‑frequency or out‑of‑distribution phenomena, and heterogeneous-device constraints. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representational, output‑level, and data-side interventions with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable, task‑aware component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with data strategies, architecture design, and complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization—rather than as a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe. Its strengths include strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks and support for privacy- or data‑limited settings; its limits include teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatches, optimization and distribution‑shift failures, and degradation on rare or fine‑grained outputs. Practical deployment requires explicit attention to what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is integrated with other compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Versatile, but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applicable family of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When designed as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline, KD routinely yields strong tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity; however, reliable deployment requires task‑aware choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and explicit mitigations for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Dependent Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and flexible family of methods for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical results across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks show KD can recover most of a teacher’s performance while delivering substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication cost. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime and selection, the choice of transfer signals, and how KD is combined with complementary compression methods. For reliable deployment, practitioners should treat KD as a task‑aware toolbox—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student carefully, addressing data or privacy constraints, and integrating pruning/quantization or architecture-aware design—while explicitly mitigating limitations such as teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Levine
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context-Dependent Tool Best Used in a Compression Portfolio

KD should be treated as a core, necessary element of practical compression pipelines but not as a standalone solution: the best results come from integrating KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and from applying context-aware design and mitigation for bias, robustness, and data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bradley

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applied approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact students. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression primitives; accordingly, KD is best treated as a configurable core of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practically driven toolbox for transferring performance from large teacher models to smaller student models across modalities and tasks. Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but gains depend strongly on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, domain shift, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Generalization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a broadly applicable paradigm that enables deployment of large models across modalities, supports privacy- and resource-constrained federated scenarios, and improves generalization when combined with task- and architecture-specific techniques. Empirical evidence shows that KD alone yields large gains for small students, while hybrid approaches that distill internal representations, use curriculum or meta-learning, augment data, or jointly optimize architecture and distillation produce state-of-the-art trade-offs between size, speed, and task performance. KD is therefore a foundational tool for modern model compression strategies and should be used in concert with complementary methods (e.g., pretraining, low-precision numerics, structural compression, and privacy-aware distillation) to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across computer vision, generative modeling, 3D rendering, graph learning, and natural language processing, researchers employ a range of distillation paradigms — including teacher-student soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, self-distillation, data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, and automated architecture search guided by teacher models — to produce smaller, faster, or more interpretable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. Practical concerns such as limited or unavailable training data, domain shifts, adversarial robustness, and the need for interpretable or low-precision models have driven specific adaptations of KD. Empirical results across tasks show that (1) distillation can greatly reduce model size or runtime with small accuracy loss, (2) internal- and feature-level matching often improves transfer beyond logits-only approaches, and (3) novel protocols (e.g., ensemble teachers, generative pseudo-replay, many-to-many layer alignment) expand KD applicability to privacy-sensitive, multimodal, and generation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance

Success requires careful design around what to transfer, how to align layers and inputs, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate bias, rare-token degradation, and teacher errors; combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search) and using task-aware curricula or projectors typically yields better accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis

papers_seen.author: Sawyer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

A range of complementary techniques — layer-wise mapping, data-free and zero-shot synthesis, self-distillation, adversarial and robust distillation, online/ensemble methods, and task-adaptive architecture search — together make distillation applicable under constraints such as limited data, privacy restrictions, heterogeneous devices, and production-scale training. I argue that adopting a portfolio of distillation strategies, chosen to match data availability and deployment constraints, yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and interpretability for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Murphy

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across vision, generation, speech, and NLP tasks, distillation methods transfer logits, intermediate representations, and task-relevant signals; when combined with complementary compression techniques they enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous-device constraints. Remaining practical challenges include selecting appropriate teacher signals, handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, and dealing with limited or private data, but a growing toolkit of task-aware, layer-wise, adversarial, and data-aware variants mitigates these issues.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Model Compression with Practical Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated family of techniques that enables production of compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when its objectives, data, and teacher-student design are matched to deployment constraints, but it is not a turnkey remedy: careful method selection and safeguards are required to avoid capacity mismatch, optimization failure modes, and transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Necessary Core and a Configurable Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when it is treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to generate or select data, and which complementary compression techniques to combine. However, KD is conditional: its reliability depends on teacher quality, data design and availability, teacher–student alignment, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors or biases. For robust, production-ready compression one should therefore treat KD as the core of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline that includes pre-training, multi-teacher or meta-teaching protocols, and deployment-aware primitives such as pruning or quantization.

papers_seen.author: Cooper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. KD methods range from simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures, and include online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data‑free variants. Empirical work shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost, but its effectiveness is context dependent: outcomes hinge on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and whether KD is combined with complementary compression primitives and deployment-aware design. Important open problems include principled signal selection for heterogeneous architectures, reliable distillation under limited or private data, mitigation of transferred biases and low-frequency failures, and automated, hardware-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, federated) together with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search, module replacement) enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD’s success is context-dependent: outcomes depend on the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit measures to mitigate bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and applying task- and data-aware design choices yields the most reliable practical results.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad set of empirical techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, recommendation, speech, graph, and generative tasks, KD variants enable substantial reductions in parameter count, latency, and memory while often retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success is context dependent: it requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data or synthetic samples to use, and how to pair KD with complementary compression methods and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include distilling in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive regimes, handling teacher–student architecture mismatch, and preserving long-tail or rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger or more complex models (teachers, ensembles, or supernets) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models (students). Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, distillation strategies include matching logits, mimicking intermediate features, adversarial generation of surrogate data, ensemble compression, and teacher-student co-training. Practical extensions address limited or private data, multi-teacher and domain-shift scenarios, and architecture search for generative models. Empirical results show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, pretraining of compact models, and task-aware feature imitation can preserve much of the teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, and that specialized methods are required for structured outputs (e.g., detection, segmentation, ranking) and domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Jenkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD supports multiple transfer targets and training protocols, is effective across modalities and tasks when designed carefully, and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. However, its empirical success is context dependent: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and domain match, and objective design, and open challenges remain around robustness, fairness, low-frequency behavior, and automated, privacy-preserving deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically essential family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Research across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and reinforcement-learning settings has produced a toolkit of transfer targets and training protocols that, when combined with complementary compression primitives, routinely yield large reductions in latency and memory with modest performance loss. KD’s success is highly context-dependent: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and careful objective and curriculum design. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preservation of low-frequency behaviors, bias transfer, and privacy-aware or data-free regimes; best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all remedy.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central but Insufficient — Advocating Integrated Compression Pipelines for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, empirically validated approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models, enabling deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. While KD reliably recovers much of teacher performance across modalities when carefully designed, it is context-sensitive: its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Consequently, KD should be treated as the core component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware distillation signals, architecture-aware adaptations, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central tool to transfer performance from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones across modalities and tasks. The field encompasses diverse mechanisms — from soft-target supervision and feature imitation to contrastive and adversarial schemes — and integrates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work highlights when and why different formulations help, how to handle limited or absent teacher data, and which practical choices matter for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific demands.

papers_seen.author: Huang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Sensitive Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and widely applicable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations across logits, features, attention and relational signals, enabling deployments under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful integration with complementary compression methods and robustness/fairness safeguards. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware element of an integrated compression pipeline yields the most reliable real‑world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Component of Hybrid Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students. While KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and supports deployment under compute, latency, and privacy constraints, its reliability depends on task-aware choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as a configurable core within hybrid compression pipelines, paired with complementary techniques and explicit safeguards to address robustness, fairness, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized models by transferring information from larger or alternative teacher models. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online mutual distillation, ensemble-to-student distillation, cross-task distillation, and teacher-aware or student-aware training. Beyond the canonical logit-matching objective, modern work distills intermediate representations, relational and contrastive structures, and task-specific signals to improve accuracy, robustness, fairness, privacy, generation, and inference latency. Empirical results across computer vision, speech, machine translation, retrieval, graph learning, and routing problems show KD can both compress models without large accuracy loss and improve distilled students in multiple dimensions (robustness, fairness, generalization, and deployment cost). However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled knowledge (logits vs features vs relations), data complexity, and careful training strategies (sample selection, curriculum, annealing, or joint teacher-student learning). This synthesis summarizes methods, motivations, practical techniques, and empirical patterns observed across recent studies.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of objectives (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) has been developed and applied across vision, language, retrieval, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection (or synthesis), and task‑aware design choices. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and principled methods for heterogeneous architectures and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. KD encompasses logits-based, feature- and representation-level, multi-teacher, online, self-distillation, and privacy-aware variants, and its effectiveness depends on choosing what to transfer, matching student capacity to teacher signals, and integrating complementary compression and training practices. When combined with architecture-aware design, augmentation or synthetic-data generation, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols, KD enables deployable models across resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile, multi-faceted toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD variants transfer information via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, contrastive or adversarial objectives, and can operate in offline, online, self-distillation, or data‑free regimes. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher’s accuracy while producing meaningful reductions in parameters, latency, memory, and communication cost. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on matching distilled signals to the task and student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines treat KD as a configurable component within a broader compression and deployment strategy that explicitly addresses teacher imperfection, distribution shift, rare behaviors, privacy, and architecture heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional, and Integrative Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential method for producing compact models from larger teachers across modalities in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and inductive biases that yield substantial gains in latency, memory, and often accuracy. However, KD has concrete failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias transfer, and distribution shift—that limit its effectiveness when used alone. The strongest, most reliable outcomes arise when KD is treated as a configurable core of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that combines careful teacher engineering, targeted distillation signals, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Curtis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse toolkit of distillation objectives and training protocols has been developed, and KD is most effective when treated as a configurable element within an integrated compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design and complementary primitives (e.g., pruning, quantization). Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and selection of distillation data (or reliable synthesis strategies), and careful protocol design to mitigate robustness, fairness, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Empirical work across vision, speech, language, multimodal and graph domains shows KD can retain much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory when combined with complementary compression tools. However, real-world success requires careful choice of teacher signals, data strategies, and optimization protocols to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and modality or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Settings, and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies are now widespread across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and specialized settings (federated, few-shot, multi-modal, generative). Research has advanced along multiple axes: what to transfer (logits, features, attention, latent modules), how to shape the transfer (sample selection, adversarially-informed examples, curriculum, teacher ensembles, meta-learning), and special protocols for constrained environments (federated/black-box, few-shot, on-device inference). Empirical work shows KD can substantially close the performance gap between small and large models, enable practical deployment of generative and discriminative models, and, when extended, transfer robustness and interpretability. Remaining challenges include error propagation from teachers (especially for low-frequency phenomena), limitations under data heterogeneity in federated settings, and task-specific design choices for complex outputs (e.g., detection, segmentation, set outputs), motivating continued work on tailored distillation objectives and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, efficient students by transferring information from teachers via outputs, internal representations, or relational signals. KD is broadly applicable across modalities and settings and is most effective when combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, important practical and theoretical challenges remain—teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity or scarcity, transferred biases, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy constraints—motivating targeted algorithmic and systems-level remedies and further study.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: The Efficacy and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into efficient students across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and reinforcement learning). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while offering substantial inference speedups and parameter reductions, and can be enhanced by targeted techniques (data augmentation, intermediate-layer matching, multi-teacher schedules, contrastive objectives, and meta-learning). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends strongly on distillation procedure, data complexity, teacher–student alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation objectives and data strategies that address robustness, limited-data regimes, privacy/federation, and modality-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression comprise a diverse set of techniques to produce smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger or auxiliary models. Research spans supervised teacher-student frameworks, self-distillation, multi-teacher and task-adaptive compression, and distillation combined with pruning, architecture search, adversarial training, and data augmentation. Practical work demonstrates benefits across vision, multimodal, graph, and NLP tasks, while theoretical analyses connect distillation to label smoothing, ensemble behavior, and bias–variance tradeoffs. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and modalities, preserving robustness and privacy, and handling low-resource or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels — soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives — and in many training protocols (offline/online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free/zero‑shot schemes). Empirical results across vision and language show that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and appropriate data or synthesis strategies are addressed. Practical application treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of integrated compression pipelines (often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search), while explicit attention is required for limits such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, bias transfer, and degraded modeling of rare outputs.

papers_seen.author: Craig
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. Across modalities and tasks, a diverse toolbox of distillation targets and training protocols has been developed and combined with complementary compression methods to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable practical deployment, but success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability, and explicit measures to mitigate failure modes such as bias transfer, optimization gaps, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from larger or auxiliary teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Its practical value is greatest when integrated with complementary compression primitives and when adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. However, KD also has clear limits—teacher–student capacity gaps, data scarcity or mismatch, and transferred biases or robustness failures—that require targeted mitigation and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical technique for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. It supports many transfer mechanisms and deployment scenarios but is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression and robustness practices. I argue KD should be treated as a first‑class, configurable element of integrated compression pipelines rather than a one‑shot cure.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft targets/logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals, contrastive or adversarial objectives) and in varied protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and federated regimes). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal domains shows KD frequently restores a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends critically on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data strategy, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as teacher-error propagation, bias transfer, and degraded low‑frequency behaviour. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and careful data/objective choices—to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthetic Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—matching teacher logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployment commonly integrates KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Key challenges include propagation of teacher errors, degradation on low-frequency or structured outputs, data and domain mismatch, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. The KD toolbox includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and a range of training protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free or privacy-aware workflows). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), matched to teacher and student capacities, and adapted to available data and deployment constraints. While KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints, its success is context-dependent and limited by issues such as capacity mismatch, data scarcity, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena. Continued work is needed on principled theory of transferable signals, data-efficient and privacy-preserving protocols, and automated, hardware-aware co‑design of teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile set of techniques for transferring behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities, but its practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and careful mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded low-frequency behavior, and distribution shift. Therefore KD should be treated as a configurable core component of integrated compression workflows—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies—rather than a turnkey, standalone solution.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and powerful technique for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for deploying high-performing deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Work in this area has progressed beyond the original formulation of training a small student to match a teacher's output probabilities: modern approaches distill internal representations, perform many-to-many layer alignment, operate without access to original training data, combine multiple teachers or ensembles, and adapt to particular architectures and tasks (including graph networks, detectors, generative models, and language models). Practical concerns such as data heterogeneity, privacy guarantees, and robustness to distribution shift have motivated methods that use synthetic data, private perturbations, generative replay, and federated or online distillation protocols. The field continues to trade off fidelity to teacher behavior, compactness, task specificity, and deployability, with task-adaptive compression and representation-alignment methods emerging as especially effective for NLP and other structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad and practical set of techniques for transferring behaviors and representations from larger or otherwise stronger models (teachers) to smaller or more constrained models (students). KD has been adapted across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, speech, graph learning, reinforcement and lifelong learning—yielding work on algorithmic variants (self-distillation, multi-teacher, curriculum, adversarial, relational and loss-function innovations), data- and privacy-aware designs, and hardware-aware/low-precision deployments. Empirical work demonstrates KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher performance, but theoretical and optimization limits remain: students often cannot perfectly match teachers and training/data choices matter greatly. Practical advances address these limits through better supervision signals, input-side design (data augmentation), alternate discrepancy measures, and privacy/communication constraints. The field continues to move toward more efficient, fair, private and domain-robust distilled models suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Versatile but Insufficient Alone — Practical Position and Best Practices for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques that transfers information from larger or composite teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and sometimes improve generalization. KD methods span logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and many teacher/student configurations. While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity, the data used for transfer, and integration with complementary compression methods; successful deployments therefore treat KD as a core component of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than as a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more specialized ones. This synthesis summarizes methods for transferring output-level and internal representations, architectural and layer-wise strategies for compression, training variants (e.g., self-supervised, adversarial, few-shot, online, and federated settings), and applications across NLP, vision, generative models, graph learning, and distributed systems. It highlights empirical findings on when distillation is most effective, techniques to preserve or improve robustness and fairness, and practical strategies for heterogeneous and latency-sensitive deployments. Gaps and recurring challenges are identified to guide future work.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online or self-distillation—are combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves most teacher performance while enabling lower-latency, lower-memory, and privacy-aware deployment, but its success depends critically on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategies, and safeguards against transferred biases or degraded performance on rare phenomena; these dependencies motivate configurable, task-aware KD pipelines rather than one-size-fits-all recipes.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — An Argument for Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely adopted approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Empirical evidence across modalities shows KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of transferred signals, and availability or synthesis of appropriate data. For robust, fair, and production-ready compression, KD should operate as a configurable core within integrated pipelines that combine representation matching, data strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer adaptation).

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Pragmatic, but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a multifaceted framework—spanning soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational objectives, selective sample policies, and data-side interventions—KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and task structure, integrating KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), and explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, low-frequency token degradation, and data scarcity. KD should therefore be a first-class component in compression pipelines, applied conditionally and engineered around task- and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Methods and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural models and transferring knowledge from high-capacity teachers to compact students across vision, language, multimodal, and generative settings. Research has diversified beyond the original logits-based recipes into feature- and layer-level matching, many-to-many layer mappings, self-supervised distillation, data-free and online KD, task- and domain-adaptive compression, and combinations with architecture search and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs involving teacher quality, the role of soft targets as regularizers, and practical constraints such as limited data, privacy, and inference latency. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical patterns, and open directions drawn from the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A broad set of objectives and protocols—logit-level supervision, feature/attention alignment, relational and contrastive signals, adversarial or synthesized-data methods, and online or multi-teacher schemes—has been developed and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and targeted engineering (layer mapping, projectors, curriculum), and remaining challenges include teacher-bias propagation, data-domain mismatch, optimization instability, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression That Must Be Task‑Aware and Integrated
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core technique that is combined with task-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and that explicitly mitigates risks such as bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving—and sometimes improving—task performance. KD methods operate at logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision boundaries and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. KD delivers strong practical benefits across modalities and tasks but requires careful teacher–student alignment, attention to data and privacy constraints, and complementary techniques to address capacity gaps, domain shift, and rare-token behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models. KD has grown from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, privacy), but its success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment and capacity, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.
