papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Guidance, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers into compact students. KD methods operate at multiple levels—from soft-label (logit) matching to feature-, attention-, and relation-level transfers—and have been adapted to many training and deployment protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free, and federated schemes). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and recommendation shows that KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and distillation data are properly matched. In practice, KD is most effective when used as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, pretraining, data augmentation, and careful layer alignment. Remaining challenges include handling teacher biases and errors, preserving low-frequency or minority behaviors, operating under data absence or strict privacy constraints, and automating teacher–student design for heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation Is Essential but Context‑Sensitive for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely adopted toolkit for producing compact models that approach the performance of larger teachers. KD routinely delivers favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities when it is chosen and configured with attention to what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and the available data regime. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded long‑tail/low‑frequency behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger models to smaller ones. KD enables production of compact, fast models that retain much of a larger model's performance across tasks and modalities, and it can be adapted to constraints such as limited or private data, heterogeneous devices, and deployment latency. A principled KD practice chooses what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to generate or select data, and which complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to combine with distillation. Properly applied, KD is a practical and general component of modern model-deployment toolkits; misapplied, it can propagate teacher errors or fail when data or teacher–student alignment is poor.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has evolved from simple logits-matching into a configurable toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance when applied with task-aware objectives, careful teacher–student alignment, and appropriate data strategies; however, important failure modes remain (teacher quality, student capacity, limited data, distribution shift, and propagation of biases), motivating integrated pipelines and targeted mitigation strategies for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential but Insufficient — A Practical Position for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central, practically proven strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and deployable students across vision and language tasks. While distilled students often recover much of teacher performance, distillation alone is not a complete solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and careful selection of what to transfer. In practice, distillation should be treated as a configurable core of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that integrates complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), explicit fairness and robustness interventions, and data strategies ranging from augmentation to data-free synthesis.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework that reliably produces compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives—have been shown across vision, language, recommendation, and generative tasks to reduce latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not a singular cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data choices, and objective design, and it can propagate biases or fail on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, combined with architecture-aware mapping, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a central, practical toolkit for shrinking large neural models while preserving functionality for deployment, adaptation, and efficiency in deep learning and natural language processing. Research has developed a broad set of distillation objectives and training protocols, applied these techniques across modalities and structured tasks, and integrated KD with complementary compression methods. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance and enable new use cases (on-device inference, privacy-aware releases, multi-teacher ensembles, and task adaptation), while ongoing challenges include teacher imperfection, data heterogeneity, transferring fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, and principled guarantees for fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for producing compact models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and cross-device constraints when applied with task-aware choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to align teacher and student. However, its success is conditional: careful selection of teacher signals, attention to data regimes and fairness, and integration with complementary compression methods are required for reliable real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. It operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals, contrastive and adversarial objectives) and is most effective when tailored to the task, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and explicit protocols to mitigate failure modes such as teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the transfer of biases or private information. Responsible application requires task-aware teacher–student design, data strategies (including data-free or few-shot methods when necessary), and monitoring for degraded behavior on low-frequency or structured outputs.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking model size and latency while preserving performance across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation, and federated settings. Research has expanded beyond the original logits-matching paradigm into feature mimicking, many-to-many layer mapping, teacher engineering, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and task-adaptive compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights important interactions between data complexity, teacher strength, inductive bias, and augmentation strategies, and identifies practical challenges including model-heterogeneity, data heterogeneity, and the need for robust data-free methods. The field increasingly emphasizes not only how to distill but also what to distill (logits, features, inter-class relations, view- or task-specific knowledge) and how to adapt distillation to application constraints (privacy, federated settings, domain shifts, resource budgets).

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD has been adapted across logits-, feature-, and relation-level objectives, combined with complementary compression primitives, and applied in specialized settings (federated, data-free, recommender, and generative). Its practical value is substantial, but realizing that value requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate failure modes such as teacher bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Miles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential framework for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and natural language settings. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free or generative) enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application of KD requires task‑ and data‑aware choices and is most reliable when combined with complementary compression methods and explicit mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger, often ensemble, teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature, attention, relational and contrastive objectives—and across protocols including offline, online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, curriculum-guided, and data‑free regimes. Empirical work shows KD routinely improves student efficiency–accuracy trade‑offs when combined with deployment‑aware choices and complementary compression methods. However, reliable deployment requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regime, optimization and capacity gaps, and risks such as bias transfer and degraded modeling of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring information from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, and other modalities KD variants (logits/soft-targets, intermediate features, attention or relational transfers, and data‑synthesis/data‑free approaches) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of a teacher’s performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful data or privacy strategies—and when practitioners attend to teacher–student compatibility, data regime, and task constraints. Known limitations include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, sensitivity to distribution shift and rare/low-frequency phenomena, and optimization or alignment challenges that require method selection and safeguards tailored to deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practically oriented set of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants transfer information at the level of logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and are commonly combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance under resource or privacy constraints, but success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and match of transfer data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as teacher error/bias propagation, degraded modeling of rare phenomena, and sensitivity to distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware component within an integrated compression pipeline yields the most robust, deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, pragmatic framework for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teachers into compact students. KD methods span soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and variants for online, multi-teacher, data‑free, federated, and self‑distillation regimes. The most reliable deployments treat KD not as a single recipe but as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context‑Dependent Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of larger teachers' performance. KD should be treated as a first‑order component of compression pipelines, but it is not sufficient on its own: reliable deployment requires task‑aware objective selection, attention to teacher–student compatibility and data regimes, and combination with complementary compression and privacy techniques.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible, but Not Panacea Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students and for transferring task- or modality-specific capabilities. KD supports many transfer targets and training protocols and can be combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. However, reliable outcomes require careful teacher–student design, attention to data and privacy constraints, and targeted solutions for failure modes such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and preserved low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Sawyer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models. KD variants include matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention, relational and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture/architecture-search, and data strategies), KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, outcomes are context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and training design materially shape success. Practical use treats KD as a configurable component within integrated compression pipelines rather than a turnkey algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Adaptation, Privacy, and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single compression recipe: it is a flexible family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from one set of models to another. KD enables production of compact, fast models that retain much of a larger model's performance, and it can be adapted to address domain shift, limited or private data, modality-specific constraints, and even fairness or robustness objectives. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of model deployment pipelines across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and sequential tasks) and that careful selection among KD variants (logit, feature, ensemble, online, adversarial, data-free, teacher-free, and task-aware distillation) lets practitioners balance accuracy, latency, privacy, and fairness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Frank
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Modern KD goes well beyond matching soft logits: it includes intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self-distillation and multi-teacher regimes, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies. Practical limits—teacher–student capacity and optimization mismatch, teacher errors and bias propagation, domain shift, and scarce or private data—motivate task-aware design, layer-mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-preserving approaches.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applied family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations across modalities to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and integration with complementary compression methods; careful, task‑aware design yields the most reliable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and generative tasks. When designed with attention to what is transferred (logits, features, attention, or generated data), data strategy, and teacher–student alignment, KD routinely yields substantial inference and memory gains while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is bounded by data availability, teacher quality, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors, so it is best used as part of an integrated compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Bautista
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted technique for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free/self‑distillation), and is effective across modalities. However, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as a configurable element within integrated, task‑aware compression pipelines that combine distillation with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies) and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer behavior and representations from larger, more expensive models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining task performance. Across modalities and tasks, research has developed many complementary mechanisms — soft-label mimicry, intermediate representation matching, teacher-student curriculum designs, self-distillation, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- or generator-based transfer, and domain- or modality-specific adaptations — to balance accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can recover most teacher performance (and in some settings even surpass it) while enabling deployment on constrained hardware and improving reproducibility and privacy. Success depends on the distillation targets, the teacher-student pairing and training regime, the use of auxiliary data or synthetic examples, and task-specific modifications.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of methods for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD techniques operate at multiple levels—from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures—and in varied protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware data and optimization strategies, KD routinely produces compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Key open problems include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under distribution shift and heterogeneous architectures, preservation of low‑frequency/long‑tail behaviors, and privacy/fairness‑aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Brown

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Conditional, and Best Used in Hybrid Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable, and Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. When combined with architecture-aware design, layer- and feature-level objectives, adversarial or relational losses, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, NAS), KD enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss and can sometimes improve generalization. KD also faces clear limits—teacher bias, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and optimization instability—that require task-aware curricula, multi-teacher or ensemble strategies, and careful selection of distilled signals. This paper argues that KD should be the first-line instrument in compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP, provided practitioners adopt principled protocols that address known failure modes and integrate KD with complementary methods for the target deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models. Across modalities and tasks KD enables major reductions in inference cost and model size while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. The family of approaches includes logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and multi-teacher or self-distillation workflows. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and preparation, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods. Common application areas include classification, sequence modeling, generation, multimodal transfer, and domain adaptation; persistent challenges include capacity mismatches, propagation of teacher errors or biases, preserving rare or long-tail behavior, and privacy-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gallegos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Configurable Core of Hybrid Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and highly practical class of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers. Its many variants—soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free generation—make KD applicable across vision, language, reinforcement learning, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a universal solution: its reliability depends on careful matching of distilled signals to student capacity, data strategy, and targeted mitigations for bias, rare-case behavior, and distribution shift. The most dependable deployments treat KD as a configurable core within hybrid compression pipelines that combine representation-aware distillation objectives with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curriculum/data strategies, and privacy- or fairness-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, latency, and communication while attempting to preserve task performance. The literature characterizes a wide taxonomy of distillation targets and protocols, documents strong empirical gains when KD is carefully configured, and emphasizes that KD is most reliable when integrated into hybrid compression pipelines that address teacher–student alignment, data regime, and deployment constraints. Known limitations include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and bias, difficulties under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and instability under distribution shift; current best practice is task- and deployment-aware application of KD combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure, and decision-boundary or synthetic-data signals), training protocols (single/multi-teacher, online/self-distillation, task- and layer-aware schedules), and architecture-aware adaptations (projectors, layer mapping, and combinations with pruning/quantization/NAS) has been developed. Empirically, properly designed distillation pipelines recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, and can be combined with complementary compression methods to meet device and domain requirements. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps, teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift and data scarcity (including privacy- and data-free regimes), and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, KD techniques (logits, feature/attention matching, relational objectives, adversarial and data‑free protocols, and ensemble/online schemes) often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when paired with appropriate data strategies, pretraining, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD has concrete limits — teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, rare‑token degradation, and failures under distribution shift or scarce/private data — which motivate task‑aware design, multi‑signal objectives, and integration with other compression primitives. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, domain examples, practical guidelines, and open challenges documented in the selected literature.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, a diverse set of transfer targets and training protocols has emerged — from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures, and even using synthesized or privacy-aware pseudo-data. Best results typically come from combining multiple distilled signals, aligning teacher and student architectures (or adding projector layers), and integrating KD with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. Despite broad empirical success, persistent challenges include handling distribution shift and low-frequency behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, safeguarding privacy and fairness, and automating principled teacher selection. This synthesis condenses prevailing methods, empirical patterns, practical guidance, and open research directions documented in the supplied literature.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation Is Essential but Context‑Sensitive for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely adopted toolkit for producing compact models that approach the performance of larger teachers. KD routinely delivers favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities when it is chosen and configured with attention to what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and the available data regime. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded long‑tail/low‑frequency behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Landry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Dependent Tool That Must Be Integrated for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and generative domains. Empirical evidence shows KD can recover much of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its effectiveness is strongly context dependent: it hinges on what signals are transferred, teacher and student capacity and alignment, availability and composition of data, and mitigation of robustness, fairness, and low‑frequency behavior issues. Therefore, KD should be treated as a first‑line, configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation‑aware distillation with data strategies, projector or layer‑mapping modules, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to produce robust, deployable compact models.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. A broad set of methods—logit-level transfer, feature- and relation-level matching, adversarial and data-free protocols, and task-aware adaptations—enables KD to serve as a first-order component of practical compression pipelines. However, its success is conditional on teacher–student design, data regime, what is distilled, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted framework for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. Methods span soft-label (logit) matching, alignment of internal representations and attention patterns, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols; KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative modeling shows KD can dramatically reduce compute and memory with modest accuracy loss (and sometimes improvements), but outcomes depend on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific design. Important open issues include principled theory for different transfer objectives, robust and private distillation under data heterogeneity, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses many targets and protocols and—when designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data, and complementary compression methods—regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful protocol design, combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors are required for dependable real‑world deployment.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques for transferring information from larger, ensemble, or auxiliary teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD has enabled substantial reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. Effective use of KD requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data (real, synthetic, or privacy-constrained), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Although KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, it has predictable failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, transferred biases, degraded rare-event behavior, and privacy leakage—that must be mitigated by task-aware protocols and explicit evaluation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: an Essential, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with task-aware design, KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of bias, low-frequency/fine-grained behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained student models so they retain functionality while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logits-based soft-label supervision to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware mappings, adversarial and contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or heterogeneous-device protocols. Empirical and theoretical work indicates KD often acts both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, task alignment, and careful design of objectives and model interfaces. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data scarcity or domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, principled layer-to-layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating teacher-induced biases.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across logits-based soft-targets, intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and teacher-free variants, adversarial and data-free schemes, and architecture-aware strategies, KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs in vision, language, retrieval, graphs, and generative tasks. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data and privacy constraints, and combination with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Remaining gaps include robustness under distribution shift, preserving low-frequency/long-tail behavior, mitigating teacher artifacts and bias, and devising reliable procedures when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit — from soft-label matching to representation-level, adversarial, and data-free approaches — has been developed and successfully applied across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains. Practical success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student compatibility, data regime, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and generative settings, KD variants—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention, relational and contrastive objectives, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance when designed with task-aware objectives and appropriate data strategies. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines that also leverage pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data augmentation; remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity and privacy constraints, low-frequency/long-tail phenomena, and principled layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, multimodal, and other settings. KD encompasses a family of transfer signals and training protocols that, when chosen and tuned for task constraints and student capacity, frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical deployments treat KD as a configurable component within integrated compression pipelines that also include pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies; success depends on teacher quality, the student’s capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred bias, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has evolved from simple logits-matching into a configurable toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance when applied with task-aware objectives, careful teacher–student alignment, and appropriate data strategies; however, important failure modes remain (teacher quality, student capacity, limited data, distribution shift, and propagation of biases), motivating integrated pipelines and targeted mitigation strategies for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized models by transferring information from larger or alternative teacher models. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online mutual distillation, ensemble-to-student distillation, cross-task distillation, and teacher-aware or student-aware training. Beyond the canonical logit-matching objective, modern work distills intermediate representations, relational and contrastive structures, and task-specific signals to improve accuracy, robustness, fairness, privacy, generation, and inference latency. Empirical results across computer vision, speech, machine translation, retrieval, graph learning, and routing problems show KD can both compress models without large accuracy loss and improve distilled students in multiple dimensions (robustness, fairness, generalization, and deployment cost). However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled knowledge (logits vs features vs relations), data complexity, and careful training strategies (sample selection, curriculum, annealing, or joint teacher-student learning). This synthesis summarizes methods, motivations, practical techniques, and empirical patterns observed across recent studies.

papers_seen.author: Austin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. KD methods have been adapted into many variants and protocols and show strong empirical gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, but their success is highly context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality and friendliness, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis strategy, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and distribution-shift failures. Treating KD as a configurable core component within integrated compression pipelines that combine representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) produces the most reliable practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Carson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods are diverse—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free protocols—and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware data and optimization strategies. Empirical work shows KD routinely delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but important limitations remain around teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, privacy, and reliable preservation of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. By transferring predictive behavior or internal representations, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training, KD forms an essential, configurable component of modern compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around task objectives, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints—and when combined with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely reduces inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead while preserving much of teacher performance. Yet KD is not automatic: it requires careful choices about distillation signals, architecture alignment, data strategies (including data‑free or synthetic data when originals are unavailable), and safeguards to avoid propagating teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Toolkit for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students, but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to integrate complementary compression methods. When designed as part of a task-aware pipeline—with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and privacy or fairness constraints—KD yields deployable models that retain much of teacher performance; treated naively it can propagate errors and fail under data- or capacity-mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Empirical and methodological work shows KD enables practical deployment across modalities and constrained settings, but its success depends on careful design choices, complementary compression primitives, and explicit safeguards against transferred errors and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. The literature shows a broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), training regimes (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi-teacher, and data-free methods), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks indicate distilled students can often recover most teacher performance while reducing latency and memory, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the distillation signal and data regime, and safeguards for bias and rare/low-frequency behaviors. Remaining open problems include principled theory connecting distillation choices to guarantees, reliable distillation under limited/private or heterogeneous data, and automated, task-adaptive selection of what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller student models. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, structured signals) and combines naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. Effectiveness is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and optimization design; addressing these practical dimensions is central to reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. Across modalities and tasks, KD reduces inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, available data, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Treating KD as a central, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and safeguards for bias and distributional robustness—yields the most reliable path to deployable, high-performing compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Necessity, Limitations, and a Consolidated Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high‑performing deep models in resource‑constrained settings across vision, speech, recommendation, graph, and language tasks. KD delivers large efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: teacher inference cost, data mismatches introduced by distillation, low‑frequency token degradation, privacy considerations, and heterogeneous deployment constraints each demand tailored remedies. Combining complementary strategies — multi‑teacher distillation, student‑aware teacher design, projector/feature adaptation, self‑distillation, exposure to raw data, and privacy-aware or federated KD — yields robust compressed models that approach or match teacher capabilities in practice.

papers_seen.author: Stokes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied, pragmatic toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks the field has developed a diverse taxonomy of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive structure), training protocols (offline, online/self, multi-teacher, data‑free), and integrations with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost, but practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling limited or mismatched data, and mitigating risks such as transferred biases, privacy leakage, and degraded rare-output behavior.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing and accelerating deep models by transferring knowledge from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. Beyond straightforward parameter reduction, KD is used to improve student generalization, robustness, interpretability, domain adaptation, continual learning, and to enable deployment in latency- or resource-constrained settings. The literature shows a wide variety of KD objectives (logit/soft-label matching, feature imitation, relational losses), training protocols (multi-teacher, curriculum, adversarial or zero-shot data generation, teacher-free/self-distillation), and application-specific adaptations (detection, retrieval, GANs, speech, lipreading, 3D vision, recommender systems, and NLP). Empirical results demonstrate that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance and in some cases surpass teachers on efficiency-accuracy trade-offs, but raise challenges including heterogeneous teacher-student alignment, data availability, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and transferring robustness and domain-general knowledge.
