papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, broadly applicable mechanism for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models and is essential for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or hardware‑optimal deployment: it must be designed in a task‑aware way, combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and paired with data and curriculum strategies to mitigate failure modes such as teacher bias, poor low‑frequency behavior, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable core inside an integrated compression pipeline yields the most reliable production outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Sensitive Path for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven and versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around appropriate transfer targets, teacher–student alignment, and data regimes, KD frequently enables substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on task and deployment constraints, and KD must often be combined with complementary methods and task-aware design to avoid failure modes and to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, empirically grounded toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners choose among soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-free or federated protocols; these methods are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on principled choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and targeted mitigations for transferred biases and distribution-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Applications (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged — including logits/soft-label transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search — enabling deployment across vision, speech, language, generative, and multimodal settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights gains in latency, memory, calibration, and sometimes robustness, while pointing to failure modes driven by teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distribution shift; best practice treats KD as a core element of a broader, context-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields substantial latency and memory reductions while retaining much teacher performance when it is applied as part of an integrated, task- and data-aware compression pipeline. However, KD is context-sensitive: its reliability depends on choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including synthetic or teacher-generated data), and explicit measures to avoid propagating teacher artifacts or biases.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broad, practically driven family of methods that transfer predictive behavior, internal representations, or structured information from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Techniques span logits/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, channel- and layer-wise objectives, self- and multi-teacher designs, data-free and few-shot protocols, and adversarial or generator-based data synthesis. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data and training practices, distillation often preserves much of the teacher's performance and can add functional guarantees (robustness, low-precision accuracy, privacy-aware releases). Key limitations include dependence on teacher quality, student capacity and architectural alignment, distributional mismatch or limited data, and the risk of propagating teacher errors or biases, motivating continued work on principled objectives, data strategies, and deployment-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger or differently structured models to smaller or more efficient ones, reducing computational cost and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings. Approaches vary in what is transferred (logits/soft labels, intermediate representations, feature maps, attention or decision-boundary information), how the transfer is staged (offline teacher-student, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, ensemble distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving setups), and how training data or augmentation is used. Empirical results across computer vision, speech/lipreading, retrieval, translation, reading comprehension, CTR prediction, federated learning, GANs, NAS, and Transformer compression show that appropriate combination of distillation objective, data strategy, and model design can yield large gains in efficiency with modest or no loss in accuracy. Practical factors that shape success include teacher strength and mismatch to the student, the complexity of distilled data, the role of pre-training for compact models, targeted selection or augmentation of distillation samples, and orthogonal compression techniques such as structured pruning.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger or ensemble teachers. It supports a wide range of objectives—logit-level transfer, feature- and representation-level matching, relational and adversarial objectives, and many-to-many layer mappings—and is applicable across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) and settings (offline, online, data-free, federated, multi-teacher). When combined with careful teacher-student co-design, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while also serving secondary goals such as interpretability or robustness. KD is powerful but not automatic: success depends on matching objectives to tasks, mitigating teacher-induced errors or biases, and addressing optimization and data-distribution challenges.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational constraints) and can operate in offline, online, data‑free, and federated regimes. Its empirical strengths span vision, language, speech, multimodal, and distributed training settings. However, KD is not a standalone panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals and data strategy, and explicit steps to mitigate transferred biases, low‑frequency failures, and distribution shift. The most reliable compression outcomes treat KD as the practical core of a task‑aware pipeline that integrates representation matching, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. A wide variety of distillation objectives and protocols—ranging from logits and feature matching to ensemble, adversarial, self- and teacher-free methods—have been developed and successfully applied across machine translation, retrieval, speech, recommendation, vision, and multimodal tasks. KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data complexity, and alignment between teacher and student, and it can propagate teacher errors (especially on low-frequency phenomena) unless mitigated by targeted design choices. When combined with data-centric practices (filtering, augmentation), ensemble strategies, intermediate-layer alignment, or complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization), KD provides a robust, broadly applicable framework for achieving favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, configurable practical tool for model compression in deep learning and NLP. Empirical syntheses and methodological work show KD reliably produces compact, deployable students from larger teachers across modalities, but its effectiveness is conditional on careful choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data and privacy constraints, and integration with complementary compression methods. Robust, deployable outcomes arise when KD is used as the core element of an integrated pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and explicit safeguards for distributional shift, bias, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression comprise a diverse set of techniques to produce smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger or auxiliary models. Research spans supervised teacher-student frameworks, self-distillation, multi-teacher and task-adaptive compression, and distillation combined with pruning, architecture search, adversarial training, and data augmentation. Practical work demonstrates benefits across vision, multimodal, graph, and NLP tasks, while theoretical analyses connect distillation to label smoothing, ensemble behavior, and bias–variance tradeoffs. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and modalities, preserving robustness and privacy, and handling low-resource or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, efficient students by transferring information from teachers via outputs, internal representations, or relational signals. KD is broadly applicable across modalities and settings and is most effective when combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, important practical and theoretical challenges remain—teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity or scarcity, transferred biases, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy constraints—motivating targeted algorithmic and systems-level remedies and further study.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Core of Integrated Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Treated as a configurable core of compression workflows, KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory footprint while preserving much of teacher performance when its objectives, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy are chosen to match task and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a standalone cure: reliable production deployments combine KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), targeted data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or privacy-preserving data), and explicit mitigations for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher biases, and low-frequency degradation.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The literature provides a broad toolkit of distillation targets and protocols, and shows KD is effective across classification, language modeling, translation, detection, recommendation, and retrieval when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and integration with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Open problems include principled theory, robust transfer under distribution shift or privacy constraints, heterogeneous architectures, and preserving rare or structured outputs.

papers_seen.author: Miles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential framework for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and natural language settings. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free or generative) enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application of KD requires task‑ and data‑aware choices and is most reliable when combined with complementary compression methods and explicit mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Evidence, Methods, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically validated set of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A broad toolkit—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware synthesis, and curriculum or adversarial sample selection—enables students to retain much of teacher performance across vision, language, multimodal, retrieval, and federated settings. Despite strong empirical successes, important engineering and scientific challenges remain around teacher–student alignment, data availability and synthesis, preservation of low-frequency behaviors, robustness and fairness, and principled automated design for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a central, practical toolkit for shrinking large neural models while preserving functionality for deployment, adaptation, and efficiency in deep learning and natural language processing. Research has developed a broad set of distillation objectives and training protocols, applied these techniques across modalities and structured tasks, and integrated KD with complementary compression methods. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance and enable new use cases (on-device inference, privacy-aware releases, multi-teacher ensembles, and task adaptation), while ongoing challenges include teacher imperfection, data heterogeneity, transferring fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, and principled guarantees for fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized student models. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and federated settings, KD methods—including soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial or data‑free generation, and self- or online‑distillation—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity and task requirements, selecting or synthesizing suitable data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Important limitations remain (teacher–student capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, failures on low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift), so KD is best used as a configurable component within an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline with explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a flexible set of methods for transferring information from larger or more expressive teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD spans output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocol variants such as offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, and privacy-aware workflows. In practice KD is frequently combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and must be tailored to teacher/student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; while empirical results across modalities often show students can recover much of teacher performance, important challenges remain in handling capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias and robustness, and formal theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical, Context-Aware Advocacy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across modalities and tasks. When treated as a flexible, task-aware toolbox—combining logits, feature and relational objectives, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, and data-aware input strategies—KD reliably enables deployments under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. However, KD is context-dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, signal selection, data availability, and careful alignment of teacher and student. Best results come from integrating KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and from adopting targeted practices to mitigate known failure modes such as bias transfer and failures on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, more deployable student models. KD variants—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, adversarial schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants—have been applied across vision, language, graph, generative, and federated settings. When combined with careful teacher selection, data strategies, layer mapping, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and model size, while posing important challenges around distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, bias transfer, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-target (logit) supervision to representation- and layer-wise alignment—and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-augmentation or curriculum strategies. Empirical evidence across vision, language, generative models, and retrieval shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher accuracy and can add benefits such as improved generalization or interpretability when applied carefully. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, optimization choices, and explicit handling of teacher biases and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component in a broader compression pipeline, chosen and tuned to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Practical, but Not Sufficiently Complete Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. KD techniques extend beyond logit matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, attention and projection-based mappings, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-constrained regimes (few-shot, data-free). KD reliably improves deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, and sometimes robustness or privacy), but it has concrete limits—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and task-specific design needs—that make KD most effective when integrated with complementary compression and training practices.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for transferring predictive capacity from large, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). A wide range of KD objectives and protocols have been developed — from matching teacher logits to mimicking internal features, adversarially chosen samples, and data-free or zero-shot synthesis — and these are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can recover much of the teacher's performance and, when carefully engineered, support robustness, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving releases, and practical latency- or memory-constrained deployment. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices, leaving open practical challenges around heterogeneous architectures, distribution shift, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or more complex teacher models into smaller, faster student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, privacy, or deployment. The field presents a diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free), and architecture-aware adaptations that are frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, recommendation, and control shows distilled students can recover much teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and data strategies are addressed; however, KD faces limits from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, propagation of teacher artifacts, and challenges in reliably transferring robustness, low-frequency behaviors, and fairness. Best practice treats KD as a toolbox within an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline, selecting distilled signals and data strategies according to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Spears

However, its benefits are conditional: success depends on teacher quality, data design, augmentation, and careful objective selection, and KD can transfer teacher errors or undesirable biases unless explicitly mitigated. Treating KD as a configurable toolkit—combining logit-level supervision, representation matching, data-side interventions, and deployment-aware protocols—yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large portion of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, choice of distilled signals, and availability or synthesis of training data. papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD transfers information via logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, and relational or contrastive signals, and it is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and task‑aware design choices. However, KD’s success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and explicit safeguards to avoid transferring undesirable teacher properties. Treating KD as a configurable, first‑line component of an integrated compression pipeline—rather than a plug‑and‑play cure—yields the best outcomes for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD techniques encompass output-level supervision (soft logits), representation- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, progressive module replacement, and online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost, but success is context-sensitive: it depends on teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and distribution of data (including data-free or synthesized alternatives), and careful loss and layer-mapping choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable toolbox to be combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and domain-, fairness-, or privacy-aware interventions. Remaining scientific and engineering challenges include principled selection of distillation targets, reliable distillation under limited or mismatched data, mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token degradation, theoretical understanding of when and why different KD objectives help, and automated, hardware-aware co-design for heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.'}]

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD operates at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structures—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, and translation) when adapted to task constraints. KD achieves substantial reductions in latency and model size while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit measures to mitigate transferred biases and low-frequency or out-of-distribution failures. Consequently, KD should be treated as a configurable, central component of an integrated compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional — Toward Task‑Aware, Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at many levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and supports a wide range of protocols (offline teacher→student, online co‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free or privacy‑aware schemes). Empirical evidence shows KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends on task awareness, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Best practice therefore treats KD as the configurable core of a broader compression pipeline that combines appropriate distillation objectives with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies) tailored to the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Demand-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically powerful and practically versatile approach for compressing large models and transferring behavior to smaller students. KD succeeds across modalities by matching logits, intermediate features, attention, or relational structure and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Recent work extends KD to settings with no original data, privacy constraints, heterogeneous architectures, and specialized tasks (graphs, non‑autoregressive generation, lifelong learning). However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher–student design, data strategies, and task-aware objectives, and important open problems remain (capacity mismatch, teacher bias transfer, preserving low-frequency behaviors, principled layer mapping, and rigorous theoretical understanding).

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick; it is a versatile, practically proven framework that enables resource-efficient deployment, privacy-preserving learning, cross-modal and cross-domain transfers, and even improvements in robustness. When combined with complementary techniques — feature mimicking, projector modules, teacher annealing, label-smoothing–style regularization, and data-free or federated protocols — distillation can address the main bottlenecks of modern deep and multilingual models: size, latency, heterogeneity of devices, limited or private data, and domain shift. I argue that KD should be treated as a first-class, configurable component in any strategy for compressing or adapting deep models for real-world NLP and vision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, latency, and communication while attempting to preserve task performance. The literature characterizes a wide taxonomy of distillation targets and protocols, documents strong empirical gains when KD is carefully configured, and emphasizes that KD is most reliable when integrated into hybrid compression pipelines that address teacher–student alignment, data regime, and deployment constraints. Known limitations include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and bias, difficulties under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and instability under distribution shift; current best practice is task- and deployment-aware application of KD combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Bates
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically oriented set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, latency, and communication while often retaining much of task performance. Over the past decade KD has diversified from simple logit/soft-target matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, data‑ and privacy‑aware protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but its success is highly context dependent: it depends on teacher quality and friendliness, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and choice of distillation data (or synthetic alternatives), and explicit handling of transferred biases, low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift. Practical deployments treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines, applying task‑aware objective design, layer mapping, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression (but Not a Standalone Cure)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, retrieval, detection, and healthcare shows KD routinely enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and careful objective and architecture design. Best practice treats KD as the central, configurable element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly addresses data scarcity, distribution shift, privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for deploying high-capacity deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. Methods range from transferring soft labels to matching intermediate representations, leveraging ensembles or multiple teachers, synthesizing surrogate data for data-free distillation, and integrating distillation into federated and privacy-sensitive regimes. Empirical gains have been demonstrated across computer vision, generative modeling, graph learning, and natural language processing, while theoretical work and empirical studies highlight nuanced trade-offs related to regularization, sample selection, teacher quality, and heterogeneous/distributed data. Open challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, principled teacher-student design, and compression of generative and transformer models for real-world low-latency deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Insufficient Toolbox for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD has expanded beyond simple logits matching into representation-, relation-, and data-aware methods and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, the distillation data, and mitigation of privacy, robustness, and bias risks. For real-world deployment, KD should be used as the central component of an integrated compression pipeline tailored to task and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques for transferring information from larger or richer models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). KD methods range from matching teacher output distributions to aligning internal representations and using synthesized or privatized data; they are effective across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks and are commonly integrated with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while improving inference cost, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and safeguards against propagating undesirable teacher properties. Current practice treats KD as a configurable component of wider compression pipelines rather than a single algorithm, and several methodological extensions and safeguards have been proposed to address its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to meet constraints on latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals) and across protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data-free/zero-shot). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and generative tasks shows distilled students can often recover a large fraction of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization or robustness, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and careful choice of transfer signals and training protocols. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable, task-aware component embedded within integrated compression pipelines that also include pruning, quantization, and architecture design, and they adopt targeted mitigations for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Configurable, and Insufficient Alone — A Position for Integrated, Responsible Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely used approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. I argue KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of hybrid compression pipelines: it reliably delivers major efficiency gains when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data and optimization strategies, but it is not a turnkey solution. Real-world deployment requires explicit handling of teacher–student alignment, data scarcity and privacy, bias and low-frequency behavior preservation, and evaluation under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Weeks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints and supports cross-modal and domain transfer. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and complementary compression and training practices. Reliable compression treats distillation as a core component of a broader, task-aware pipeline rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practical Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when combined with deployment-aware design choices and complementary compression tools. However, realizing robust, fair, and privacy-preserving compressed models requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and method selection.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Component of Integrated Model Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Rather than a standalone cure, KD is most effective when treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that aligns distilled signals, teacher–student capacity, and data strategy, and that combines distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Responsible deployment requires addressing known failure modes—data scarcity and distribution shift, capacity mismatch, degraded low-frequency behavior, and bias/privacy risks—through targeted remedies and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied toolkit for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD encompasses soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and schemes such as offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free distillation. Empirical work shows distilled students often preserve a large fraction of teacher performance when distillation is matched to student capacity, teacher quality, and data availability; however, reliable success requires combining KD with complementary compression methods and deliberate mitigations for capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature develops a diverse toolbox—logit/soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot protocols, and teacher-aware or student-aware training—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, multimodal) when teacher–student compatibility, data strategy, and optimization design are carefully managed; it also faces limitations arising from dataset mismatch, optimization difficulty, and propagation of teacher artifacts, especially on long-tail or low-frequency phenomena. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable component of compression and deployment workflows, tuned for task constraints and complemented by safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Frank
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Modern KD goes well beyond matching soft logits: it includes intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self-distillation and multi-teacher regimes, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies. Practical limits—teacher–student capacity and optimization mismatch, teacher errors and bias propagation, domain shift, and scarce or private data—motivate task-aware design, layer-mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-preserving approaches.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central tool to transfer performance from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones across modalities and tasks. The field encompasses diverse mechanisms — from soft-target supervision and feature imitation to contrastive and adversarial schemes — and integrates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work highlights when and why different formulations help, how to handle limited or absent teacher data, and which practical choices matter for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific demands.

papers_seen.author: Li
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Configurable, but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs by transferring soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and can operate in offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free, and privacy‑sensitive regimes. However, its effectiveness depends on deliberate choices about transfer targets, teacher–student co‑design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives; without such integration KD risks failing under teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or distribution shift, optimization challenges, and the propagation of undesirable behaviors. This position argues that KD should be treated as the core, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline: necessary for most modern deployments but insufficient on its own, and requiring targeted practices and continued research to address open challenges.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential but Insufficient — A Case for Hybrid, Task‑Aware Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, versatile technique for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers into smaller students. KD frequently recovers a large portion of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness is context-sensitive. For reliable, production‑grade compression practitioners should treat KD as a configurable core component within hybrid pipelines that combine appropriate distillation targets, teacher–student co‑design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods while explicitly mitigating teacher error propagation, low‑frequency degradation, fairness concerns, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied, practical framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. KD encompasses diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and distributional failures.

papers_seen.author: Glass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Necessary, Configurable Core of Practical Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically validated, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span output-level soft-targets, intermediate representation and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online/self-distillation protocols. When treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with targeted data, architecture, and optimization strategies, KD reliably yields favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases, optimization gaps, and distributional failures. Deployment-grade outcomes require task-aware design, complementary compression primitives, and safeguards for robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mata
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the task, data regime, and student capacity, KD routinely preserves much of teacher performance and enables deployment under compute, latency, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on careful choice of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and loss of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature-, attention- and layer-wise alignment, relational/contrastive signals, adversarial and data-free sample synthesis, and meta- or multi-teacher schemes—has been developed and applied across vision, language, retrieval, graph, and federated settings. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with task- and architecture-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, limited or private data, and optimization stability; proposed remedies emphasize task-aware filtering of teacher signals, learned teacher adaptation, layer mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool: Integrating Distillation with Representation, Data, and Architecture Strategies for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, more deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone is rarely sufficient to meet real-world deployment constraints: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention), and access to or synthesis of suitable training data. Best results arise when KD is embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level matching, projector or layer-mapping modules, data and curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Careful attention to optimization, robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors is required to avoid propagating teacher errors and to produce reliable compact models for downstream applications.

papers_seen.author: Combs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Component for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated approach for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with appropriate data strategies and complementary techniques, KD routinely delivers substantial reductions in inference cost and model size while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, choice of distilled signals, and careful handling of data- and fairness-related failure modes. Responsible, deployment-ready use therefore requires task-aware design, explicit mitigation of transfer limits, and continued research into robust, privacy-preserving, and automated distillation strategies.
