papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework that reliably produces compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives—have been shown across vision, language, recommendation, and generative tasks to reduce latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not a singular cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data choices, and objective design, and it can propagate biases or fail on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, combined with architecture-aware mapping, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring predictive behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. KD spans logits-based supervision, feature and relational matching, adversarial or synthetic data generation, and architectural or curriculum adaptations. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD can enable deployment in latency- and resource-constrained settings and sometimes yield students that match or exceed teacher performance, but it also carries risks—propagating teacher errors and biases, struggling under data scarcity or mismatch, and requiring task-specific engineering. I argue KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines, applied conditionally with targeted remedies and validated against task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have matured into a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or more private models. Across computer vision, NLP, multimodal systems, federated settings, and generative models, researchers have combined soft-label (logit) distillation, intermediate feature/hint transfer, architecture transformation, quantization, pruning, and automated search to achieve significant reductions in memory, computation, or communication while largely preserving accuracy. Empirical work demonstrates that distillation can enable high-quality low-precision models, speed up inference and training, unify heterogeneous models without shared data, and make distributed learning more communication- and privacy-efficient. The field continues to refine when and what knowledge to transfer (e.g., logits vs. features vs. attention), how to handle multiple or unreliable teachers, how to design student-friendly teachers, and how to integrate distillation with other compression methods such as pruning and search.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded family of methods for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary teacher models into compact students. Modern KD methods extend beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data‑free or synthetic‑data approaches. Empirical results across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and graph tasks show KD can recover much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and data strategies are carefully matched; practitioners therefore treat KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware training. Important limitations remain—teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, degraded modeling of rare outputs, distributional shift, privacy concerns, and theoretical gaps—motivating research on adaptive teacher selection, data synthesis, privacy-preserving protocols, and better mappings between distilled signals and student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and properties of larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and privacy-sensitive settings, KD variants transfer logits, intermediate representations, relations, or synthesized data to produce students that meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often yields favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and model size, but its success depends on data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and careful objective and training choices.

papers_seen.author: Singh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Practical Trade-offs, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, relations, or generated samples), in the availability of original training data (data-rich, data-free, federated), and in whether distillation is performed offline, online, or jointly with teacher training. Across vision, language, ranking/retrieval, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, carefully designed distillation objectives combined with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search) routinely yield compact models that approach teacher performance under practical constraints. However, the effectiveness of KD depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data selection and augmentation, and mitigation of risks such as propagated bias, privacy leakage, and poor modeling of rare phenomena. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines, using multi-teacher and confidence-weighting strategies, layer- and feature-matching, student-aware teacher design, and privacy-preserving or data-free synthesis when needed.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically driven set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or composite teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets and training protocols has been developed—soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, self- and online-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods—often integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and training design. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable component in a broader compression pipeline that must be tailored to task, data regime, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher–student soft-label transfer into a flexible set of methods that enable compact, fast, and often more robust models across vision, language, multimodal and generative settings. When designed with awareness of task constraints, data availability, and deployment demands, KD combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, layer skipping, meta-learned teachers, or generative replay) reliably yields practical gains. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a first-class, configurable component in compression pipelines: powerful and broadly applicable when paired with principled, task-centered decisions, but demand-aware and tuned to deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Carson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods are diverse—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free protocols—and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware data and optimization strategies. Empirical work shows KD routinely delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but important limitations remain around teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, privacy, and reliable preservation of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, pragmatic approach for producing smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger teacher models. KD succeeds widely across modalities and tasks when it is tailored to what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of bias, rare-token behavior, and domain shift. Best practice treats KD as a core element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression comprise a diverse set of techniques to produce smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger or auxiliary models. Research spans supervised teacher-student frameworks, self-distillation, multi-teacher and task-adaptive compression, and distillation combined with pruning, architecture search, adversarial training, and data augmentation. Practical work demonstrates benefits across vision, multimodal, graph, and NLP tasks, while theoretical analyses connect distillation to label smoothing, ensemble behavior, and bias–variance tradeoffs. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and modalities, preserving robustness and privacy, and handling low-resource or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, researchers have extended KD beyond soft-label matching to include feature- and attention-level alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, online and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Practical success depends on teacher quality and student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data strategies, and combinations with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of when particular signals help, handling heterogeneous or non-iid data in federated settings, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and reliably scaling distillation in large distributed systems.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive performance. Empirical evidence across vision, language, generative models, and retrieval shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher accuracy and can add benefits such as improved generalization or interpretability when applied carefully. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component in a broader compression pipeline, chosen and tuned to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often multi-source or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Indispensable but Task‑Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD variants have been successfully adapted across modalities and tasks, and when designed with awareness of task constraints, data availability, and student capacity, distillation yields substantial practical gains. However, KD has concrete limits—capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and failures on rare phenomena—that make it most effective when integrated into broader, task‑aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or ensemble teachers into smaller, faster, or specialized student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A broad and practical toolbox has emerged—logit/soft-label transfer, feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free/zero-shot protocols, and architecture-aware combinations with pruning, quantization, and search—that is applied across vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative settings. Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance when applied carefully, but success depends on student capacity, teacher design/quality, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices; important open problems remain in principled theory, fairness/privacy-aware protocols, heterogeneous and federated settings, and robust distillation for generative and structured-output tasks.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, widely applicable mechanism for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact models can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when its objectives, data, and mappings are chosen with the target task and student capacity in mind; but KD alone does not guarantee production-ready compression. Reliable deployment requires integrating distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), careful data and teacher selection, layer and projector design, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior transfer.

papers_seen.author: Vang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), supports online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation and data‑free regimes, and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its empirical success spans vision, language, speech, retrieval and multimodal generation, but outcomes are context‑dependent: they depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or public data), and task‑aware objective design. Documented failure modes include capacity and optimization mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, difficulty preserving low‑frequency phenomena and distributional mismatch. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and emphasizes careful signal selection, data and curriculum strategies, and targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Spencer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD operates over multiple transfer targets and training protocols, routinely improves efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives and task-aware data strategies. Although KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization or robustness, its outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability and alignment of data; consequently, KD is best treated as a configurable component of an end-to-end compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has grown from a simple teacher→student soft-target idea into a broad, task-aware toolbox for producing compact, faster, and more deployable models in deep learning and NLP. A diverse set of distillation targets and protocols (logits, intermediate representations, attention, relational and contrastive signals; offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants) together with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of teacher performance. Practical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment and capacity, data strategy, and mitigation of failure modes such as transferred errors, distribution shift, rare-output degradation, and privacy constraints. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—with task-aware signal selection, layer mappings or projectors, curriculum or sample-selection strategies, and, where needed, adversarial or synthetic-data protocols—yields the most reliable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Cain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger “teacher” models to compact “student” models. Across modalities and tasks, KD has been adapted to operate on output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures, and it can run in offline, online, multi‑teacher, or data‑free regimes. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers much of a teacher’s performance and, when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and training strategies, produces production‑ready tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity. However, KD is context‑sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, alignment of inputs and layers, data availability and distribution, and risks of transferring teacher errors or biases all shape outcomes. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline with targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Core of Practical Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for producing compact models from larger teachers across modalities and tasks. KD offers many targets and protocols—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data‑free or privacy-aware variants—that routinely improve efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and careful objective design; it therefore functions best as a configurable component inside an integrated compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, teacher adaptation, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, and Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques — spanning soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation matching, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and teacher-aware or multi-teacher strategies — repeatedly enable large reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on task and data properties, teacher–student alignment, optimization, and deployment constraints, and it works best when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, evidence-backed approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD methods — ranging from logits transfer to intermediate-feature matching, self-distillation, and selective-sample protocols — routinely enable substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: success depends on what information is transferred, teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data choices, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, KD provides a practical route to deploy high-performing models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Model Compression with Practical Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated family of techniques that enables production of compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when its objectives, data, and teacher-student design are matched to deployment constraints, but it is not a turnkey remedy: careful method selection and safeguards are required to avoid capacity mismatch, optimization failure modes, and transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and communication while preserving much of teacher performance. KD operates at multiple levels — soft targets (logits), intermediate representations, attention and relational structure, and contrastive objectives — and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, pretraining, and architecture adaptation. Practical success is conditional on teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful optimization and evaluation to avoid propagating teacher artifacts, degrading rare-case behavior, or failing under distribution shift. The field shows strong empirical gains across vision, language, speech, recommendation, generative, and multimodal tasks, while open problems remain in theory, heterogeneous architectures, privacy-aware protocols, and robust transfer of low-frequency or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficiently Complete Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical set of techniques that enables production of compact models that retain much of larger teachers' functionality across modalities and tasks. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and hardware constraints. However, distillation has concrete failure modes — propagation of teacher errors, difficulty preserving low-frequency phenomena, capacity and distribution mismatches, and privacy or robustness concerns — which require complementary methods, data strategies, and careful teacher–student design. I argue KD should be adopted as a central, configurable tool in compression workflows but not relied on alone: best practice integrates KD with representation-aware objectives, curriculum/data strategies, multi-teacher or collaborative teaching, and targeted safeguards for bias, rare-case behavior, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compressing large models for deployment and domain-specific use. Across modalities and tasks, KD can preserve much of the teacher's performance in compact students, but it must be combined with task-aware engineering—such as teacher adaptation, layer-wise selection, data augmentation, and hardware-aware pruning—to address heterogeneity, domain shift, and efficiency constraints. This article argues that KD is necessary but not sufficient: best results come from integrating KD with complementary techniques chosen for the target modality, deployment constraints, and learning scenario.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. The literature converges on a taxonomy of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive signals), protocols (offline teacher–student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free/synthetic data), and engineering integrations (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, pretraining, and data strategies). Empirical work shows KD often preserves a substantial portion of teacher performance while substantially reducing parameters, latency, and memory across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and multimodal applications, but success is context dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred biases or robustness failures. Current open problems include principled theory of what transfers, reliable distillation under distribution shift or privacy constraints, and preserving low-frequency or structured outputs in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across logits-based soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, layer-mapping or projector modules, multi- and self-distillation, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online or federated protocols, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Empirical results show KD can sometimes improve generalization and enable deployment under privacy or resource constraints, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and match, and careful design choices about what and how to transfer. Combining KD with complementary techniques (augmentation, curriculum learning, pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tailoring the distillation signals to task and deployment constraints yields the most reliable practical gains.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely used family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods have expanded from simple logits-matching to include feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free and federated protocols, and many-to-many teacher–student mappings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability or synthesis. KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Hurley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal signals from larger teacher models into smaller, resource-efficient student models. The field encompasses simple logits-based soft-target transfer as well as richer objectives that match intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and uses protocols that include offline, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—and when distillation signals, layer alignment, and training data are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks) but faces reproducible failure modes (capacity and optimization mismatch, distribution shift, degradation on low‑frequency phenomena, and propagation of teacher biases or privacy risks) that motivate targeted mitigations and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, widely applicable mechanism for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact models can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when its objectives, data, and mappings are chosen with the target task and student capacity in mind; but KD alone does not guarantee production-ready compression. Reliable deployment requires integrating distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), careful data and teacher selection, layer and projector design, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior transfer.

papers_seen.author: Fuentes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When integrated with complementary compression techniques and adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints, distillation routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. Success requires careful selection of distillation signals, alignment between teacher and student, appropriate data or synthetic examples, and explicit safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness. Distillation should therefore be treated as a configurable, central component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a plug‑and‑play solution.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural information. A broad toolkit of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline, online/self-, multi-teacher, data‑free) and engineering practices (layer mapping, projectors, curriculum, data synthesis) has been developed and routinely combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirically, distillation frequently recovers most of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and augmentation strategies, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors or low-frequency phenomena. Effective deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to integrate distillation within end-to-end compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques constitute a flexible toolkit for transferring behavior and internal structure from large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, or deployment‑specific student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations, and structured objectives) and across protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free, and federated schemes). Empirical practice shows KD often retains a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in compute, memory, and latency when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data and architecture choices. However, KD’s effectiveness is context dependent: it is sensitive to teacher quality and mismatch, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and the risk of propagating teacher artifacts (biases, low‑frequency errors). Remaining needs include principled theory linking distilled signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous or non‑i.i.d. data, and robust privacy/fairness guarantees for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or ensemble teachers into smaller, faster, or specialized student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A broad and practical toolbox has emerged—logit/soft-label transfer, feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free/zero-shot protocols, and architecture-aware combinations with pruning, quantization, and search—that is applied across vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative settings. Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance when applied carefully, but success depends on student capacity, teacher design/quality, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices; important open problems remain in principled theory, fairness/privacy-aware protocols, heterogeneous and federated settings, and robust distillation for generative and structured-output tasks.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Core of Practical Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for producing compact models from larger teachers across modalities and tasks. KD offers many targets and protocols—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data‑free or privacy-aware variants—that routinely improve efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and careful objective design; it therefore functions best as a configurable component inside an integrated compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, teacher adaptation, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. KD methods span output-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-aware or data-free protocols. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness, its success is strongly context dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability and synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy determine practical outcomes. As a result, KD should be treated as a configurable, first‑line element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, configurable family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD reduces latency, memory, and compute while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. KD encompasses many targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial/data‑free synthesis, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies appropriate to the task and deployment constraints. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as optimization difficulties, bias transfer, and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled objectives, robust/private distillation under data scarcity, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger, often ensemble or overparameterized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals, attention maps, and adversarial or generator-based surrogate data) and are widely used across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and selection of data (including synthesized or public data in privacy-sensitive settings), and how KD is combined with complementary compression methods. Key open problems include handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving low-frequency or minority phenomena, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher and objective design for optimal transfer.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Conditional, and Best Used within Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable and practically effective toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD can recover much of teacher performance, enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and be extended across logits, feature, attention, and data‑free paradigms. Its effectiveness, however, is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and selection of distillation data, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable, task‑aware component that must be combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search), data strategies, and robustness/fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are now core tools for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. The literature has expanded far beyond simple logits matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, and tight integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates broad applicability across modalities (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and generative models) and deployment contexts (edge devices, federated systems, and data-constrained settings). The main practical challenges are (1) choosing what and how to distill for a given task and student architecture, (2) coping with limited or unavailable original training data, (3) avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses (e.g., biases or low-frequency degradation), and (4) co-designing distillation with other compression primitives and hardware constraints. Progress comes from combining representational objectives, layer-mapping strategies, task-aware teacher selection, and safeguards (privacy or fairness) appropriate to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gonzales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Dependent Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable and practical family of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers, routinely recovering much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and objective design, and it must be integrated with complementary compression techniques and safeguards to mitigate risks such as teacher errors, bias transfer, and degraded low‑frequency behavior. When treated as a configurable core of a compression pipeline and validated against deployment constraints, KD typically yields the best accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger or specialized models. KD is used across domains—image classification, detection (2D and 3D), recommendation/CTR, language model compression, federated and heterogeneous-device learning, and reinforcement learning—and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or curriculum strategies. Despite strong empirical success, open problems remain in understanding when particular KD variants best transfer generalization, how to measure and mitigate transferred biases, and how to optimally combine KD with other compression primitives for different constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD operates at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structures—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, and translation) when adapted to task constraints. KD achieves substantial reductions in latency and model size while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit measures to mitigate transferred biases and low-frequency or out-of-distribution failures. Consequently, KD should be treated as a configurable, central component of an integrated compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Paul
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers while retaining much of their predictive performance. KD methods span output-level supervision, representation- and attention-level matching, curriculum and multi-teacher protocols, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Treated as a configurable core component that is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and task-aware design choices, KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs but requires targeted remedies for capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and privacy or robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy; KD is therefore best used as a first-line, integrated tool rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Not Sufficient Alone for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans many transfer targets and training protocols and often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires careful, task-aware choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability and privacy, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression tools. Treating KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline—rather than a single recipe—yields the most reliable path to deployable, efficient models.
