papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single teacher-to-student logits-matching recipe into a large, task-aware toolbox for producing compact, efficient models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Research documents many variants (soft logits, feature and relational matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, data-free and privacy-aware procedures, multi-teacher and online schemes) and shows that KD, when combined with complementary compression methods and task-specific design choices, can deliver substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining most of a teacher's performance. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, choice of transfer signals, availability and manipulation of data, student capacity, and deployment constraints; important open problems include theoretical guarantees, optimization gaps, distribution shift, privacy, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers capabilities of large models into smaller ones via indirect supervision. Methods vary by what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single, ensemble, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and practical constraints (limited data, privacy, cross-distribution generalization, modality mismatch). Empirical work across speech, vision, language, retrieval, graph, generative modeling, and medical imaging shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while gaining resource efficiency; theoretical analyses and diagnostic studies clarify mechanisms and guide designs such as projector layers, many-to-many layer mapping, and curriculum or data-augmentation strategies. Remaining challenges include distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, robust transfer of inductive biases, and principled layer-to-layer alignment for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for transferring information from large, expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, efficient models. Methods include logit-based distillation, feature- or representation-based matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher strategies, data-free and privacy-preserving approaches, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. KD has been applied across modalities and domains—vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, generative models, and healthcare—demonstrating gains in inference efficiency, robustness, generalization, and interpretability when appropriately designed. Open challenges remain around data availability, teacher–student mismatch, selection of distilled signals and samples, and principled integration with other compression techniques; recent work proposes meta-learning teachers, adaptive teacher weighting, projector modules, and task-adaptive compression as practical remedies.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and training protocols enable large reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Real-world success depends on task- and capacity-aware choices of distillation signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free and federated variants), and combination with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is powerful but conditional: it frequently yields strong trade-offs in practice but requires careful treatment of teacher quality, data regimes, and robustness or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, multimodal and generative settings. KD techniques transfer teacher behavior via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational objectives, and can be extended to data-free, privacy-preserving, and adversarial regimes. Best results arise when distillation is combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search); remaining challenges include data- or domain-limited scenarios, teacher–student mismatch, robustness and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, Configurable Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), diverse scheduling regimes (offline, online, progressive), and synergistic combination with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest loss in task performance, its success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (or synthetic/data-free strategies), and explicit measures to mitigate bias, robustness, and privacy concerns determine outcomes. Consequently, KD should be treated as a first-order, configurable tool in compression pipelines—selected and tuned according to task, data, and deployment constraints—rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Domains, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger or multi-source models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models to reduce memory, compute, and latency while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher logits to mimicking internal features, and extend to self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and adaptations for few-shot, federated, and multimodal settings. Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models shows KD can enable compact models that approach teacher accuracy, improve calibration and fairness, and make deployment on resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices practical. Ongoing challenges include selecting what to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning heterogeneous architectures, and designing KD protocols robust to limited data, domain shifts, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mccormick
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When designed with attention to which signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, and distillation-data strategies, and when combined with complementary compression primitives, KD routinely yields favorable tradeoffs between efficiency and performance across modalities. However, KD is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on mitigating failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare‑token behavior, teacher–student mismatch, and distributional shift. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware element of integrated compression pipelines — rather than a turnkey replacement for other techniques — produces the most reproducible deployments and points to principled research directions for robust, privacy‑aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes what the provided literature collectively reports about knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques: commonly used distillation objectives and training protocols, empirical patterns of when and how KD helps across modalities, practical constraints and failure modes (data availability, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency/structured outputs, privacy and bias transfer), and targeted solutions (data-free/zero-shot distillation, teacher engineering, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and combinations with pruning/quantization and architecture search). The goal is to give a concise map of methods, observed trade-offs, and open problems for researchers and practitioners working on compressing or adapting large models for resource- or deployment-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Gregory
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central but Insufficient — A Practical Position for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD methods span logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and specialized protocols (online, multi-teacher, data-free). Empirical evidence shows KD routinely preserves much of teacher performance and enables substantial efficiency gains across modalities and tasks, but its success is conditional on teacher–student alignment, data regime, and task-specific design choices. Therefore, KD should be treated as a configurable, core component of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models. KD succeeds most reliably when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline: practitioners should select appropriate transfer targets (logits, features, attention, relational signals), adapt objectives to student capacity and data regime, and combine distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies). While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities, it is not a universal cure—limitations such as teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and the risk of propagating biases require targeted mitigations and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. Across modalities and tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and relation-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial schemes, and data‑free generation—regularly produce large size and latency reductions with modest performance loss when designed in a task- and deployment-aware way. Practical success is conditional on teacher quality, data regime, teacher–student alignment, and safeguards against propagation of undesirable teacher properties; addressing open problems (robust data-free distillation, theory of transfer, fairness and privacy) requires integrating KD into end-to-end compression pipelines and co-designing students, objectives, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Approaches vary by what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel statistics, or decision-boundary information), by whether original training data are available, and by whether the goal is efficiency, robustness, privacy, or domain adaptation. Empirical work across vision, multimodal, speech, and natural language tasks shows that careful choices of transfer targets, loss formulations, teacher ensembles, and training schedules can yield compact models that approach — and in some cases match or exceed — teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties that prevent perfect belief matching, distribution-shift and heterogeneity issues in federated or data-free settings, and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. KD methods span output-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-aware or data-free protocols. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness, its success is strongly context dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability and synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy determine practical outcomes. As a result, KD should be treated as a configurable, first‑line element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, more deployable student models. KD variants—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, adversarial schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants—have been applied across vision, language, graph, generative, and federated settings. When combined with careful teacher selection, data strategies, layer mapping, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and model size, while posing important challenges around distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, bias transfer, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployable systems under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods span soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs, but reliable deployment requires task- and data-aware design, attention to teacher–student compatibility, and combination with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Mendez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models. Over the past decade the field has diversified well beyond simple logits matching to include intermediate-feature and relational objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, data-free or generator-based approaches, and task-aware engineering such as layer mapping and projector modules. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows that KD can produce substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often retaining much of a teacher’s performance; achieving reliable results requires careful choice of distillation signals, alignment between teacher and student, and integration with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. Important open problems remain around principled design, robust transfer under data scarcity and distribution shift, and mitigation of transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Huang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Sensitive Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and widely applicable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations across logits, features, attention and relational signals, enabling deployments under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful integration with complementary compression methods and robustness/fairness safeguards. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware element of an integrated compression pipeline yields the most reliable real‑world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. Across modalities and tasks, KD reduces inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, available data, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Treating KD as a central, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and safeguards for bias and distributional robustness—yields the most reliable path to deployable, high-performing compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated, practical family of methods for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD methods include soft-logit/temperature matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, adversarial and data‑free schemes, and online/self‑distillation variants. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when training choices account for teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and deployment constraints. KD often preserves most teacher performance and can improve student generalization, but it can also transfer teacher biases or degrade rare-token behavior; therefore it should be treated as a configurable, task-aware component of end-to-end compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically powerful and versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations via multiple signals (logits, features, attention, relational objectives) and supports a wide range of training protocols and data regimes. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on careful, task‑aware design, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and combination with complementary compression methods to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and potential bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ramsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective and widely adopted framework for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD is best understood as a configurable core technique: it provides many transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, contrastive objectives, and synthesized data), and—when combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search and coupled with task‑aware data strategies—can enable large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data regime, and explicit measures for robustness, privacy, and fairness strongly shape outcomes. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as an essential but non‑turnkey component of integrated compression pipelines, selecting targets, mapping strategies, and safeguards to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Luna
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, flexible approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational signals, or synthesized inputs to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical success is highly context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and complementary compression choices. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution. Persistent challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, robust transfer of rare behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous deployments.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression — Powerful but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods (soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational objectives, and data- or generator-based synthesis) repeatedly enable large reductions in model size and inference cost when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression primitives. However, KD's success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degraded modeling of rare phenomena. Treating KD as a configurable component of integrated compression pipelines, rather than a one-shot cure, leads to more reliable and deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded family of methods for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary teacher models into compact students. Modern KD methods extend beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data‑free or synthetic‑data approaches. Empirical results across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and graph tasks show KD can recover much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and data strategies are carefully matched; practitioners therefore treat KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware training. Important limitations remain—teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, degraded modeling of rare outputs, distributional shift, privacy concerns, and theoretical gaps—motivating research on adaptive teacher selection, data synthesis, privacy-preserving protocols, and better mappings between distilled signals and student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Universal Tool for Model Compression and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique that enables model compression, deployment efficiency, and task- or domain-specific adaptation across a wide range of deep learning settings. Empirical work shows KD can reduce memory and compute with small accuracy loss, enable low-precision inference, compress specialized generative or multi-modal models, and provide routes to interpretability and data- or privacy-constrained scenarios. Best results arise when KD is adapted to the task (choice of objectives, teacher ensembles, data augmentation, or data-free strategies) and when student architectures or training protocols explicitly account for heterogeneity between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods include soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free protocols, and teacher/student co-design; in practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware engineering. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under limited or mismatched data, mitigation of transferred biases and degraded rare-token behavior, principled selection of distillation targets, and automated hardware-aware co-design.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. It supports multiple information-transfer mechanisms (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and can be adapted to constrained settings (limited data, privacy, heterogeneous devices). KD is most effective when used as part of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or pretraining—and when practitioners mitigate known failure modes such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, or teacher–student mismatch. With careful design choices (what to transfer, how to align layers, which data to use), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while largely preserving task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Austin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. KD methods have been adapted into many variants and protocols and show strong empirical gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, but their success is highly context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality and friendliness, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis strategy, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and distribution-shift failures. Treating KD as a configurable core component within integrated compression pipelines that combine representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) produces the most reliable practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving—sometimes even improving—task performance. Across vision, language, speech, recommender, and multimodal tasks, tailored distillation pipelines enable compact models suitable for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Walker

When combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely enables large reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Its empirical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and synthesis strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Nelson

While KD is not a universal cure, its flexibility and empirical success make it a first-choice strategy for compression when combined with careful design choices about teacher quality, transfer signals, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez

papers_seen.author: Fischer

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, widely applied family of methods that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, more deployable student models. papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD techniques encompass output-level supervision (soft logits), representation- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, progressive module replacement, and online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost, but success is context-sensitive: it depends on teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and distribution of data (including data-free or synthesized alternatives), and careful loss and layer-mapping choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable toolbox to be combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and domain-, fairness-, or privacy-aware interventions. Remaining scientific and engineering challenges include principled selection of distillation targets, reliable distillation under limited or mismatched data, mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token degradation, theoretical understanding of when and why different KD objectives help, and automated, hardware-aware co-design for heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for transferring information from large, expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, efficient models. Methods include logit-based distillation, feature- or representation-based matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher strategies, data-free and privacy-preserving approaches, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. KD has been applied across modalities and domains—vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, generative models, and healthcare—demonstrating gains in inference efficiency, robustness, generalization, and interpretability when appropriately designed. Open challenges remain around data availability, teacher–student mismatch, selection of distilled signals and samples, and principled integration with other compression techniques; recent work proposes meta-learning teachers, adaptive teacher weighting, projector modules, and task-adaptive compression as practical remedies.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework that reliably produces compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives—have been shown across vision, language, recommendation, and generative tasks to reduce latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not a singular cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data choices, and objective design, and it can propagate biases or fail on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, combined with architecture-aware mapping, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from larger, more accurate, or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Over the past decade KD has broadened from matching teacher output probabilities to a diverse set of objectives that include internal representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and online or self-distillation schedules. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training pipelines, distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transferred errors, biases, and distributional brittleness.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational constraints) and can operate in offline, online, data‑free, and federated regimes. Its empirical strengths span vision, language, speech, multimodal, and distributed training settings. However, KD is not a standalone panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals and data strategy, and explicit steps to mitigate transferred biases, low‑frequency failures, and distribution shift. The most reliable compression outcomes treat KD as the practical core of a task‑aware pipeline that integrates representation matching, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible set of techniques to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, generative modeling, and structured prediction domains, KD variants — including logit transfer, feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations — provide concrete trade-offs between model size, compute, and accuracy. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, low-precision numerics, pruning and layer skipping, or teacher training tailored to students, distillation yields practical, deployable models applicable to constrained hardware and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool for Compression, Robustness, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into efficient students while also serving as a lever for regularization, robustness, privacy, fairness, interpretability, and continual/multi-task learning. When applied thoughtfully—combining soft-label distillation with feature- and representation-level matching, layer mapping, attention or projector modules, and task-aware curricula—KD can produce lightweight models that approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance on constrained devices and specialized tasks. However, KD is not automatic: optimization difficulties, data heterogeneity, and mismatches in the information transferred (e.g., for low-frequency tokens or internal features) limit its effectiveness unless complemented by targeted methodological choices. I argue that KD should be treated as a principled toolbox rather than a single recipe: choose distillation targets (outputs, features, internal representations), mapping strategies (many-to-many layer mapping, attention, projectors), and auxiliary safeguards (privacy-preserving noise, fairness interventions, adversarial distillation) to align compression goals with safety and utility requirements.

papers_seen.author: Huang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Sensitive Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and widely applicable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations across logits, features, attention and relational signals, enabling deployments under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful integration with complementary compression methods and robustness/fairness safeguards. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware element of an integrated compression pipeline yields the most reliable real‑world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses a wide family of techniques — from soft‑target/logit matching to intermediate feature, attention and relational alignment, as well as online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation and data‑free protocols — and routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when matched to teacher/student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, teacher–student compatibility, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and it requires explicit strategies to mitigate transferred biases, degraded low‑frequency behavior, and distribution shift. Treated as a configurable, integrated component of compression pipelines, KD enables practical deployment across modalities while pointing to open challenges in theory, privacy, and robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Cole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely reduces inference cost and parameter counts while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core element within integrated compression pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and explicit robustness and fairness evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Barker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad and practical toolkit—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free protocols, and multi-teacher or self-distillation schemes—has been developed and applied across vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative tasks. KD frequently produces compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on careful design choices for distillation targets, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Singh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Practical Trade-offs, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, relations, or generated samples), in the availability of original training data (data-rich, data-free, federated), and in whether distillation is performed offline, online, or jointly with teacher training. Across vision, language, ranking/retrieval, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, carefully designed distillation objectives combined with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search) routinely yield compact models that approach teacher performance under practical constraints. However, the effectiveness of KD depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data selection and augmentation, and mitigation of risks such as propagated bias, privacy leakage, and poor modeling of rare phenomena. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines, using multi-teacher and confidence-weighting strategies, layer- and feature-matching, student-aware teacher design, and privacy-preserving or data-free synthesis when needed.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds across modalities and deployment constraints when its design — what to transfer, which teacher(s), the data regime, and complementary compression primitives — is matched to the task and student capacity. However, KD is not a panacea: careful co-design and safeguards are required to avoid propagating teacher errors, to preserve rare or low-frequency behaviors, and to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied framework for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact student models. A wide range of distillation objectives (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive losses), training protocols (offline, online/self-, multi-teacher), and data strategies (full-data, limited-data, data-free, and privacy-aware synthesis) have been proposed and combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical studies show KD often recovers much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and suitable data strategies are available, but KD is context-dependent and must be integrated with task-aware design choices to manage limits related to teacher–student mismatch, optimization, data scarcity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses logit/soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its practical strengths include enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, improving generalization and some robustness properties, and serving as a core component of compression pipelines when used with task-aware design choices. At the same time, KD exhibits clear failure modes—teacher–student mismatch, bias transfer, poor preservation of low-frequency behaviors, and sensitivity to data availability and domain shift—that motivate complementary methods and targeted research into robust, privacy-preserving, and automated distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and broadly effective set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD reduces latency, memory, and communication costs while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance; its toolbox includes soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols ranging from offline to online, multi-teacher, and data-free distillation. However, KD’s success is conditional on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Responsible, robust deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, configurable family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD reduces latency, memory, and compute while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. KD encompasses many targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial/data‑free synthesis, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies appropriate to the task and deployment constraints. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as optimization difficulties, bias transfer, and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled objectives, robust/private distillation under data scarcity, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Stanley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. KD spans matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free protocols, and multi- or online-teacher schemes. Empirical work shows KD typically recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can interact positively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and explicit mitigation of bias, distribution shift, and low-frequency failures. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across modalities and tasks, distillation is used to transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from larger, more accurate teachers to smaller, faster students; it also appears within automated model search, pruning and distributed training workflows. Work in this area spans logit matching, representation-level objectives, data-free and few-shot regimes, multi-/online-teacher schemes, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Empirical results demonstrate that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy while enabling large reductions in memory and compute, but limitations remain around optimization, data availability, and the preservation or mitigation of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: The Case for Task- and Data-Aware Knowledge Distillation: Principles, Pitfalls, and Practical Extensions for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical success across vision, language, graph, and generative models depends not only on the generic teacher→student paradigm but on task-aware selection of transferred information, choices about data access (including data-free and privacy-preserving variants), and the use of auxiliary techniques (adversarial training, ensembling, pruning, and architecture search). When these dimensions are addressed explicitly, distillation can produce compact models that approach teacher performance while offering improved robustness, interpretability, or resource-efficiency. However, naive distillation can fail due to optimization difficulties, domain shift, and heterogeneous teacher-student mismatches, so practitioners must adopt targeted strategies that consider the learning objective, available data, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, multimodal tasks and specialized settings (e.g., 3D detection, ranking, medical imaging), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data or synthetic alternatives are used; KD is most effective when used as a configurable component combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from one or more teacher models to a student. A rich taxonomy of KD methods exists—output (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, self- and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and adversarial/sample-generation approaches—applied across classification, generation, translation, retrieval, graph learning, detection, and federated settings. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the form of transferred signals, the availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and choices about layer mapping and optimization. Outstanding challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, distribution shift, and reliably distilling structured or rare outputs; promising directions emphasize task-aware signal selection, many-to-many layer mappings, adversarial/data-free synthesis, teacher-free or meta-learned schemes, and tighter integration of KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central tool to transfer performance from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones across modalities and tasks. The field encompasses diverse mechanisms — from soft-target supervision and feature imitation to contrastive and adversarial schemes — and integrates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work highlights when and why different formulations help, how to handle limited or absent teacher data, and which practical choices matter for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific demands.

papers_seen.author: Mendoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Effects, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, flexible framework for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals) and protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free, and curriculum-driven). Empirical work demonstrates KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all. Key open directions include principled selection of signals to transfer, robust privacy-preserving distillation, automation of deployment-aware pipelines, and reliable compression of large transformer and generative models.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models by transferring behavior from larger teacher models. When used as a configurable, task- and deployment-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline, KD routinely reduces latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Its practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression primitives; persistent challenges include bias transfer, handling low-frequency phenomena, distribution shift, and automating signal selection.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Camacho
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When applied as a task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline—alongside pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies—KD frequently yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, and the data regime.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable collection of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary models (“teachers”) into smaller, more deployable models (“students”). Over the last decade KD has diversified beyond simple soft-label matching to include feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data‑free protocols, and online or self-distillation schemes. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers much of a teacher’s performance while enabling reductions in parameters, latency, and memory, but reliable deployment requires task‑aware design, careful handling of data and teacher imperfections, and integration with complementary compression methods.
